# `.codex/` — constellation-root

<!-- GENERATED BY .claude/scripts/codex_sync.py — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND -->

The Codex control plane for this repo. It is a **projection** of `.claude/`,
not an independent configuration. `.claude/` is canonical; edit there and
re-run:

```bash
~/GitHub/.claude/scripts/codex_sync.py --repo /Users/omarkhalil/GitHub
```

| Codex artefact | Projected from | Count |
| -------------- | -------------- | ----- |
| `agents/*.toml` | `.claude/agents/*.md` | 7 |
| `skills/<n>` (symlink) | `.claude/skills/<n>/` | 8 |
| `skills/<n>/SKILL.md` | `.claude/commands/<n>.md` | 22 |
| `hooks.json` | `.claude/settings.json` `hooks` | 4 events |
| `config.toml` | `.claude/settings.json` model/effort/permissions/env | — |
| `rules/default.rules` | `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.deny` | 0 |

Hook *scripts* are never copied. `hooks.json` invokes the same
`.claude/hooks/` files Claude Code uses, through `hook_shim.py`, which
re-applies Claude's argument-level matchers and exports
`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`.

## Two things Codex needs that Claude does not

1. **Project trust.** Codex ignores a project-local `config.toml`,
   `hooks.json` and `rules/` until the project is trusted. Run
   `~/GitHub/.claude/scripts/codex_sync.py --trust` once.
2. **Hook trust.** Codex refuses to run hooks until you approve them
   interactively: open `codex` in this repo, run `/hooks`, choose
   *Trust all and continue*. Until then hooks are silently skipped —
   including the secret scanner and the commit gate.

## Invocation differences

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| skill | model-invoked, or `/name` | `$name` |
| slash command | `/name` | no equivalent — projected as `$name` |
| subagent | Task tool / agent name | ask Codex to spawn `<name>` |

## Local additions

Anything you want for Codex only, with no Claude counterpart, goes in
`.codex/local/`. The projection never reads it and never deletes it.
